name: Amon
charge: Sacrificing to all the carved images his father had made; humbling not himself as his father had humbled himself, but trespassing more and more
summary: Amon began to reign at twenty-two, reigned two years, and brought back all the idols his father Manasseh had served, without the humbling his father came to at the end (2 Kings 21:19-22; 2 Chronicles 33:21-23). He trespassed more and more, and his own servants conspired against him and killed him in his house; the people of the land killed the conspirators and made his son Josiah king (2 Kings 21:23-24).
offenseFull: Every time a king tried to remove the idolatry, Israel found its way back to folly; the Lord speaks peace to His people, but they are not to turn again to folly (Psalm 85:8). Manasseh reigned fifty-five years, and at most the last few were spent trying to put things right. Amon was twenty-two when he took the throne, so most of his life had been spent under his father’s worst years, watching the rituals and the orgies of Baal worship. That was what he was raised in, and as soon as his father died he brought it all back as if Manasseh had never tried to undo it. He did evil as his father had done, walked in all his ways, served the idols his father served, and forsook the Lord God of his fathers (2 Kings 21:19-22).

Chronicles sets him beside his father on purpose: he sacrificed to all the carved images Manasseh had made, and did not humble himself as his father had, but trespassed more and more (2 Chronicles 33:22-23). Ezekiel describes exactly this: a just man who has a son that is a robber, a shedder of blood, who eats on the mountains and lifts his eyes to idols. It does not matter that the father repented; that son will surely die, and his blood is on himself (Ezekiel 18:10-13). The idols Amon served are named in Josiah’s cleansing: vessels made for Baal, for the grove and for all the host of heaven, idolatrous priests burning incense to the sun, moon and planets, and houses of the sodomites by the house of the Lord (2 Kings 23:4-7). Baal worship came with sexual rites, and it is thriving today under the name of Christianity and liberty, down to the daily horoscope beside the scripture. The worship of idols is the beginning, the cause and the end of all evil, and with it come blood, theft, adultery and men slaying one another treacherously (Wisdom of Solomon 14:23-27). Because sentence against an evil work is not carried out speedily, men’s hearts are set to do evil (Ecclesiastes 8:11), and his sins abounded to his own destruction.
judgmentFull: The servants of Amon, the people he kept close, conspired against him and killed the king in his own house (2 Kings 21:23). That was the fruit of his own work: the idolatry he enforced brought with it the spirit of slaying one another treacherously, and it came back on him. The traitors did not escape either; the people of the land killed all who had conspired against the king and made Josiah his son king in his place (2 Kings 21:24). Treason was not tolerated.

The power of the earth is in the hand of the Lord, and in due time He sets over it one that is profitable (Ecclesiasticus 10:4). Wicked rulership lasts only so long. The throne passed to a boy of eight who, while he was still young, began to seek the God of David his father (2 Chronicles 34:1-3). Ben Sira says that all the kings of Judah were defective, for they forsook the law, except David, Hezekiah and Josiah (Ecclesiasticus 49:4). Grandfather, father and son stood in a row: the one who went past the Amorites and then humbled himself, the one who saw it and trespassed more and more, and the one who turned to the Lord with all his heart.

text.text: Amon was twenty and two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Meshullemeth, the daughter of Haruz of Jotbah.
And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, as his father Manasseh did.
And he walked in all the way that his father walked in, and served the idols that his father served, and worshipped them:
And he forsook the Lord God of his fathers, and walked not in the way of the Lord.
Amon was two and twenty years old when he began to reign, and reigned two years in Jerusalem.
But he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, as did Manasseh his father: for Amon sacrificed unto all the carved images which Manasseh his father had made, and served them;
And humbled not himself before the Lord, as Manasseh his father had humbled himself; but Amon trespassed more and more.
And the servants of Amon conspired against him, and slew the king in his own house.
And the people of the land slew all them that had conspired against king Amon; and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his stead.
I will hear what God the Lord will speak: for he will speak peace unto his people, and to his saints: but let them not turn again to folly.
But he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, as did Manasseh his father: for Amon sacrificed unto all the carved images which Manasseh his father had made, and served them;
And humbled not himself before the Lord, as Manasseh his father had humbled himself; but Amon trespassed more and more.
If he beget a son that is a robber, a shedder of blood, and that doeth the like to any one of these things,
And that doeth not any of those duties, but even hath eaten upon the mountains, and defiled his neighbour’s wife,
Hath oppressed the poor and needy, hath spoiled by violence, hath not restored the pledge, and hath lifted up his eyes to the idols, hath committed abomination,
Hath given forth upon usury, and hath taken increase: shall he then live? he shall not live: he hath done all these abominations; he shall surely die; his blood shall be upon him.

And the king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, and the priests of the second order, and the keepers of the door, to bring forth out of the temple of the Lord all the vessels that were made for Baal, and for the grove, and for all the host of heaven: and he burned them without Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron, and carried the ashes of them unto Beth–el.

And he put down the idolatrous priests, whom the kings of Judah had ordained to burn incense in the high places in the cities of Judah, and in the places round about Jerusalem; them also that burned incense unto Baal, to the sun, and to the moon, and to the planets, and to all the host of heaven.

And he brought out the grove from the house of the Lord, without Jerusalem, unto the brook Kidron, and burned it at the brook Kidron, and stamped it small to powder, and cast the powder thereof upon the graves of the children of the people.
And he brake down the houses of the sodomites, that were by the house of the Lord, where the women wove hangings for the grove.
For whilst they slew their children in sacrifices, or used secret ceremonies, or made revellings of strange rites;
They kept neither lives nor marriages any longer undefiled: but either one slew another traitorously, or grieved him by adultery.
So that there reigned in all men without exception blood, manslaughter, theft, and dissimulation, corruption, unfaithfulness, tumults, perjury,
Disquieting of good men, forgetfulness of good turns, defiling of souls, changing of kind, disorder in marriages, adultery, and shameless uncleanness.
For the worshipping of idols not to be named is the beginning, the cause, and the end, of all evil.
Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.
And the servants of Amon conspired against him, and slew the king in his own house.
And the people of the land slew all them that had conspired against king Amon; and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his stead.
The power of the earth is in the hand of the Lord, and in due time he will set over it one that is profitable.
Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem one and thirty years.
And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the ways of David his father, and declined neither to the right hand, nor to the left.

For in the eighth year of his reign, while he was yet young, he began to seek after the God of David his father: and in the twelfth year he began to purge Judah and Jerusalem from the high places, and the groves, and the carved images, and the molten images.
All, except David and Ezekias and Josias, were defective: for they forsook the law of the most High, even the kings of Juda failed.
